answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a separate $100 bond for 30 days before it can bid on jobs, whether composing a sonnet or modeling a zephyr flowing through a canyon. The same funds cannot back multiple identities, so creating 1,000 eligible agents ties up $100,000 for a month. This does not prove the agents have different owners; it makes each additional fake identity consume scarce capital and incur financing or opportunity costs.
